chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: FRQ 2 Evidence-Based Question (EBQ) — 7 points — Set 1: factors influencing performance
chunks.content: AP Psychology FRQ 2 is the Evidence-Based Question (EBQ), 7 points, based on three sources. Scored by parts A–C. Part A [1]: propose a specific, defensible claim that responds to the prompt. Part B [up to 3]: support the claim with evidence from EACH of the sources, applying psychological concepts (one point per source used accurately and applied). Part C [up to 3]: explain how the evidence supports the claim using psychological reasoning and address the argument's scope/limitations. Set 1 topic: factors that influence performance. The concept must be applied to the sources/claim — a definition alone does not earn the point. Common failure: a claim that only restates the prompt; citing a source without applying a psychological concept; reasoning that restates evidence rather than linking it to the claim.

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: EBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2A, 7/7
chunks.content: EBQ (Set 1) scored 7/7 — a defensible claim (A), evidence applied from all three sources (B, 3 points), and reasoning that links the evidence to the claim and addresses scope (C, 3 points). Full-credit model for the Evidence-Based Question.

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: EBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2B, 5/7
chunks.content: EBQ (Set 1) scored 5/7 — earned the claim and most evidence/reasoning points but lost about two, commonly one source not applied with a concept or a reasoning point that restated evidence. Illustrates a strong EBQ short of full evidence/reasoning credit.

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: EBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2C, 1/7
chunks.content: EBQ (Set 1) scored 1/7 — earned only about one point (typically the claim), with sources not applied via psychological concepts and reasoning that did not connect evidence to the claim. Illustrates a claim without developed, source-grounded support.
